This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
ORDER The applicant has filed this third application u/S 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

His second application for the same relief was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file after recording of evidence of Doctor who have examined the prosecutrix vide order dated 31.3.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.54852/2022.

The applicant has been arrested by Police Station Karariya Chauraha, District Vidisha in connection with crime No. 156/2022 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(i), 354, 354-B,

1 509, 376-A, 376B of IPC and Section 3/4 and 5m, 5h, 6 of the POCSO Act.
As per prosecution case, the applicant took the minor prosecutrix in his house for playing with her and thereafter, committed sexual assault by finger penetration.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All the material witnesses including her sister, mother and doctor have been examined.

It is further argued that the entire prosecution story is highly improbable and suspicious because prosecution witness PW-3 sister of prosecutrix has admitted in her statement at para-12 that maternal uncle of prosecutrix had eloped the minor sister of applicant on account of which the families of applicant and prosecutrix are not in good terms and they do not go to the houses of each other.
In these circumstances, the story of prosecution that the applicant took the prosecutrix in front of her mother and sister in his house for playing with her is highly improbable.
It is further argued that her sister had told her the things to be deposed.

It is further argued that PW-4 Doctor Archana Patel who had examined the prosecutrix has spefically mentioned that no injury was found on the private part of the prosecutrix whereas according to the prosecution, the penetration was caused by finger.
As per the Doctor.
other injuries may be caused on account of fall.
In these circumstances, so also in the light of the fact that all the material witnesses have been examined;
therefore, the question of influencing them does not arise.
Applicant is in custody since 18.06.2022.
He is having no criminal antecedents.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Vidisha.
Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no likelihood of his absconsion, if released on bail.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 1.00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
